findings.title: Negative offset queryset slicing will crash with AssertionError
findings.body: Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing — `queryset[-5:96]` raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment on line 876 ('The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically') is factually incorrect. When `enable_advanced_features=True` and a user supplies a cursor with a negative offset (e.g., `cursor=0:-5:0`), this code path will execute `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`, causing an unhandled 500 error. This is trivially triggerable by any user who passes the `optimized_pagination=true` parameter and has the required access level.

findings.title: BasePaginator change allows negative offsets when is_prev=True, causing crashes
findings.body: The modified line `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` explicitly passes negative offsets through to the queryset slice when `cursor.is_prev` is True. Since `is_prev` is user-controlled (third component of the cursor string parsed in `Cursor.from_string`), any user can craft a cursor like `0:-10:1` to trigger a Django `AssertionError` on the queryset slice. The original code had the same latent issue but this change makes it intentional and removes the `max(0, ...)` guard for the `is_prev` path, which is a regression for all endpoints using `BasePaginator` (including `DateTimePaginator`).

findings.title: No validation that cursor offset is non-negative in Cursor.from_string
findings.body: `Cursor.from_string` parses the offset as `int(bits[1])` without validating it is >= 0. Since cursor strings are user-supplied input (from the `cursor` query parameter), a malicious or malformed cursor with a negative offset (e.g., `0:-100:0`) will be accepted. Combined with the paginator changes in this PR that explicitly allow negative offsets through to queryset slicing, this creates a denial-of-service vector where any authenticated user can trigger 500 errors on paginated endpoints.

findings.title: Access control check may be insufficient and could raise AttributeError
findings.body: The expression `organization_context.member.has_global_access` will raise `AttributeError` if `organization_context.member` is `None` (which can happen in certain edge cases with the RPC organization context). Additionally, `has_global_access` grants this feature to org managers/admins, not just owners — meaning a broader set of users can trigger the buggy negative-offset code path. If the intent is to restrict this to superusers only during initial rollout, the `has_global_access` check should be removed.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator docstring and comments are misleading
findings.body: The class docstring claims it provides 'Negative offset support for efficient reverse pagination' and 'Optimized query path for large datasets', but the implementation is functionally identical to the existing `Paginator` class except for the broken negative-offset handling. There is no actual performance optimization (no query plan changes, no index hints, no limit pushdown). The misleading documentation could cause future developers to believe this class provides real performance benefits and adopt it elsewhere.
